job: Rear brake shoes replacement (drum brakes, one axle)
unit: one set of rear brake shoes (both rear wheels), fitted, with the existing drums reused. Not included: new drums, machining the drums, wheel cylinders, a hardware (spring) kit unless the shoe price says it includes one, brake fluid service
held_reason: First attempt, 2026-11-20. Only the truck class has a labor range, and both ends are a parts seller's approximate install time, not a book time. Economy has both parts ends but no usable labor time: every maker bulletin found either adds a drum or wheel cylinders to the shoes, prints the time with no unit, or points to the maker's labor guide without printing a time. Midsize has no sourced example. Luxury is null because no luxury-make vehicle with rear drum service brakes was found. The truck aftermarket price is null because none of the three retailer pages loaded says the shoes are new. Needs: a shoes-only time with a unit for an economy and a midsize car, a midsize example with two parts sources, and a truck retailer page that says new.

finding: New job, so there is no live range to judge, and this file is not ready to show a range. Built totals use parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks). Only the truck class can be partly built: on a 2016 Toyota Tacoma the labor is 1 to 2 hours ($120-$320), and with the shoes at Toyota's list price of $94.96 the total is about $215-$415; no low total with aftermarket shoes is given because none of the three retailer pages ($62.99, $64.48, $69.99) says the shoes are new. Economy (2015 Corolla): parts are $34.10 aftermarket to $89.64 Toyota list, but no total is built because no shoes-only labor time with a unit was found. Midsize: nothing sourced. Luxury: null, because no luxury-make vehicle with rear drum service brakes was found. How solid the labor times are: weak. The Tacoma figures are a parts seller's approximate install times (1 hour on one listing, 2 hours on another), not book times. The maker bulletins found do not give a clean shoes-only time: GM allows 0.9 hr on a Chevrolet Cruze for one new drum plus the shoe kit, FCA allows 1.2 hr on a Ram ProMaster City for shoes plus both wheel cylinders, Toyota prints 1.1 to 1.2 for Tacoma shoes with new drums but gives no unit, and GM's Sonic bulletin and Nissan's bulletins point to the labor guide without printing a time. Those cross-checks all sit between about 1 and 1.5 hours, which is consistent with the truck range but does not replace a stated time. Against the outside estimates: the partial truck total ($215-$415) overlaps RepairPal ($314-$397) and sits below Jerry ($350-$550) and YourMechanic's Tacoma table ($398-$509); RepairPal assumes $173-$253 of labor, which at $120-$160/hr is roughly 1.1 to 2.1 hours.
extras: A quote often adds new drums or machining the existing drums, a hardware (spring and adjuster) kit, wheel cylinders if they are leaking, a brake fluid bleed or flush when the hydraulics are opened, parking brake adjustment, brake cleaner and shop supplies, an inspection or diagnosis fee, and sales tax. The dealer catalogs loaded list a Corolla drum at $117.41 and wheel cylinder at $65.18, and a Tacoma drum at $165.16 and wheel cylinder at $61.53, each at list price.
